newsitem.title: GERMANY: German govt broadly agrees 3-bln mark cut - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: German govt broadly agrees 3-bln mark cut - spokesman.

text.p: The German government has reached "broad agreement" on making savings of around three billion marks in the 1997 budget, a spokesman told reporters on Friday after Chancellor Helmut Kohl chaired a cabinet meeting.
Spokesman Peter Haussmann declined to give details of the cuts, which will now be submitted to the three parties of Kohl's centre-right coalition for approval.

Party chiefs from Kohl's 14-year coalition of his Christian Democrats (CDU), Finance Minister Theo Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU) and the Free Democrats (FDP) will meet late Sunday to discuss the cuts.
Waigel is seeking to squeeze Germany's budget deficit within the Maastricht treaty's three percent limit of economic output to qualify next year for European Monetary Union.
A Finance Ministry spokesman said that the cuts took into account new tax revenue forecasts which were due for imminent publication.
Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said after the meeting that the military budget had been spared further big cuts, and that the amount to be saved was "nearer 200 million marks than 400 million marks".
No decision, Ruehe said, has yet been reached on placing an order to enable production of the Eurofighter combat aircraft to begin next year.
Labour Minister Norbert Bluem confirmed that he would seek savings of one billion marks at the Federal Labour Office, but said he was pleased there would be cut in unemployment benefits.
